voiceSessions.transcript: Hello, um, I am an engineer and, like, I want to improve my speaking, you know, because public speaking makes me nervous.

strengths: Steady speaking attempt with 22 words expressed.
Willingness to keep talking through hesitation.
Clear attempt to address the prompt directly.
weaknesses: Detected 3 filler words ("um", "like", "you know"). Practice comfortable silent pauses instead.
Speaking pace was 38 WPM (ideal conversational pace is 110–140 WPM). Aim for smoother transitions between thoughts.
pronunciationTips: Focus on the clear ending of consonants in words like "project", "talked", "confident".
Use natural intonation: raise your pitch slightly when asking questions and lower it at the end of statements.
recommendations: Record yourself answering this same question a second time without looking at any notes.
When you feel the urge to say "um" or "like", close your mouth and take a gentle one-second breath.

videoSessions.transcript: Good morning everyone. Today I am honored to share our team breakthrough in clean energy. We faced numerous obstacles, but perseverance allowed us to deliver real results.

strengths: Maintained good composure in front of the camera.
Spoke for 50 seconds with continuous engagement.
Addressed the scenario with a direct and clear opening.
weaknesses: Continue working on vocal projection and dynamic pitch variation.
stageFearTips: Remember: Public speaking is an acquired mechanical skill, not an innate talent. Every practice session rewires your comfort zone.
Focus on the listener rather than your own anxiety. When your goal is to help or inform the other person, self-consciousness naturally decreases.
Take three slow diaphragmatic breaths before clicking record to lower heart rate.
bodyLanguageAdvice: Keep eye contact near the upper third of your screen where the camera lens is located.
Maintain an open posture with relaxed shoulders and occasional natural hand gestures to emphasize key ideas.
recommendations: Try advancing to Level 4 in this scenario to practice under slightly more dynamic conditions.
Re-record with a 5-second silence buffer before you begin speaking to center your thoughts.
